verdict.rationale: Claude Design's own docs say it turns static mockups into shareable, interactive prototypes without code, PRs or code review, refined through conversation and direct edits. Nothing documents designer-controlled wiring of screens, such as defining triggers, transitions or overlays; interactivity appears to be AI-generated rather than configured by the designer. missing for 10: explicit screen-to-screen linking controls, trigger/interaction configuration, transition/animation settings between screens, overlay/modal support, independent hands-on corroboration of clickable prototype flows

support.subject: As a designer, I can wire screens into clickable prototypes with triggers, transitions, and overlays — no code required

citations.quote: Turn a static mockup into a shareable, interactive prototype you can test with real people. No PRs, no code review.
Designers can turn static mockups into easily-shareable interactive prototypes to gather feedback and user-test, without code review or PRs.
you refine through conversation, inline comments, direct edits, or custom sliders (made by Claude) until it's right
